description: Sayadieh Fish Rice is a beloved Middle Eastern seafood dish, celebrated for its aromatic spiced rice and tender, perfectly cooked fish. The star of this culinary masterpiece is the deeply caramelized onions, which lend a unique sweetness and rich color to the rice. This traditional recipe brings together simple ingredients to create a truly unforgettable and comforting meal.

instructions.title: Prepare the Fish and Rice
instructions.text: Pat fish fillets dry with paper towels and season generously on both sides with salt and black pepper. Wash the Basmati rice thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. Soak the washed rice in fresh water for 15 minutes, then drain well.

instructions.title: Caramelize the Onions
instructions.text: In a large heavy-bottomed pot or deep skillet, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat. Add the thinly sliced onions and cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 15-20 minutes. Continue cooking until the onions are deeply golden brown and caramelized. Remove about half of the caramelized onions from the pot and set them aside to use as garnish later.

instructions.title: Sear the Fish
instructions.text: With the remaining onions and oil in the pot, gently place the seasoned fish fillets. Sear them for 2-3 minutes per side until they are lightly golden brown and slightly cooked on the outside. Carefully remove the seared fish from the pot and set it aside; it will finish cooking later with the rice.

instructions.title: Prepare the Spiced Broth
instructions.text: To the pot with the remaining caramelized onions, add the cumin powder, coriander powder, allspice, turmeric powder, and the remaining black pepper. Stir and cook for about 1 minute until the spices are fragrant. Pour in the fish broth and bring the mixture to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot to incorporate their flavor. Taste the broth and adjust the salt if necessary.

instructions.title: Cook the Rice and Fish
instructions.text: Add the drained rice to the simmering spiced broth in the pot. Gently arrange the seared fish fillets on top of the rice. Bring the liquid back to a boil, then immediately reduce the heat to very low. Cover the pot tightly with a lid and let it cook undisturbed for 18-20 minutes, or until all the liquid has been absorbed and the rice is tender.

instructions.title: Rest, Garnish, and Serve
instructions.text: Once the rice is cooked, turn off the heat and let the Sayadieh rest, still covered, for 10 minutes. This allows the flavors to meld and the rice to steam perfectly. Gently fluff the rice with a fork, being careful not to break the fish fillets. Garnish generously with the reserved caramelized onions, toasted pine nuts (if using), and fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side.

tips: For the best caramelized onions, cook them slowly over medium-low heat. Patience is key to developing their deep, sweet flavor and rich color without burning them.
Choose a firm white fish like cod, snapper, or halibut that holds its shape well during cooking. Avoid delicate fish varieties that might flake too easily and disappear into the rice.
To toast pine nuts, dry-fry them in a small non-stick pan over medium heat for 2-3 minutes until golden and fragrant. Watch them closely as they can burn very quickly.
